item.title: Somnia
item.description: Every human culture that has ever existed has had a word for dreams. The ancient Egyptians built temples where the sick would sleep on sacred ground, waiting for a vision that would tell them how to heal. The Greeks called it incubation — sleeping inside the oracle. Aboriginal Australians don’t separate the Dreaming from reality at all. Jung spent a lifetime mapping the unconscious and concluded that what appears in sleep is the self attempting to speak to itself in the only language honest enough: symbol, feeling, image.
